correctness.rationale: Proof first identifies exactly one normalized vector u per symmetric rank-one idempotent uu^T, and shows distinct projections commute iff orthogonal. For every partial orthonormal frame, the nondegenerate complement is alternating iff the standard canonical vector belongs to the span, proving terminality. The explicit 1-dimensional plus hyperbolic-plane conversion establishes all nonalternating form normal forms. Odd- and even-dimensional isometry orders are derived with a symplectic quotient and kernel, and orbit-stabilizer gives exact clique and maximal-clique multiplicities including d=0 and all parity boundaries. A standalone verifier exhausts every clique against literal field/matrix arithmetic in ten finite cases; unrestricted conclusions rely on proof not experiments.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison with accessible primary results and semantic published research database records did not find the exact nonalternating, normalized rank-one projection commuting graph or its all-size terminal-frame and clique formulas. The established projection equivalence and symplectic/isometry group orders are treated as known inputs or rederived, not claimed novel. Iosevich-Senger asymptotic tuple counts are not this exact enumeration; the 2025 quadratic-form graph has alternating polar adjacency in characteristic two and cannot dominate the nonalternating graph. Priorities remain bounded and the 2016 close orthogonal-graph source was available in abstract only.

value.rationale: In characteristic two, partial rank-one symmetric projection commuting families can be inclusion-maximal far below the full size n, despite available orthonormal bases. The new explicit terminality criterion shows every parity-allowed nonmaximal size occurs, determines the unique odd-n isolated projection and exact counts for every size/extension-field degree. Full clique polynomial complements this maximal-only spectrum. These are natural graph invariants distinguishing local maximality from global maximality, not arbitrary unmotivated small-case enumeration.
